label: GO-phase last-trial S2/rare evidence raises n; S1-rewarded lowers it
terms: (phase == GO) * (prev_state == 2) ;; (phase == GO) * (prev_state == 1) * (prev_reward == 1) ;; (phase == GO) * (prev_state == 2) * (prev_reward == 1) ;; (phase == GO) * (prev_common == 0) ;; (phase == D1) * (prev_state == 1) * (prev_reward == 0) ;; (phase == D1) * (prev_reward == 1) ;; (phase == GO) * np.tanh(choice / 3) ;; (phase == D2) * (action == 2)
explanation: Raw candidate n of unit 8. Timing dominates (R^2 0.83: about +0.9 at D1/D2, falling at GO over the episode, and D1 also falls late in the episode). Beyond timing, the variance is mostly at GO and is set by the last trial: it is higher after reaching S2 (+0.35), higher after a rare transition (+0.19), and lower after a rewarded trial (S1 rewarded -0.33, S2 rewarded -0.26 relative to S2 alone). So after a1 S1 r it is lowest (about -0.45) and after rare or S2-unrewarded trials it is highest (+0.3 to +0.4). It also rises when the GO policy leans toward a2 (tanh(choice) weight -0.09). At D1 it drops after S1-unrewarded trials (-0.22) and rises a little after any reward (+0.13). At D2 it is slightly higher when a2 was chosen (+0.11). The trial before adds little (<0.01), and this trial's reward, the hidden good state and value add little. All terms are observed or model outputs, none future. Dev R^2 beyond timing 0.61, test 0.60 (all ceiling 0.70, all observed 0.66). Not captured: the late-episode D1 dips during runs of unrewarded trials.

issues: Minor wording problem: 'D1 rises a little after any reward (+0.13)'. In the raw D1 residuals the rise comes mostly from S2-rewarded trials (+0.12 / +0.11); S1-rewarded trials are about zero (a1 S1 r +0.055, a2 S1 r -0.018), and misses over-predicts D1 after a2 S1 r by -0.097. Still, a D1 term for 'any reward' scores better than one for 'S2 rewarded only' (test 0.602 vs 0.587), so the term itself is fine.

The tanh(choice) term at GO is weak and its shape is not monotone. The GO residual by policy decile peaks at decile 2 (+0.24); decile 0 (most a2) is only +0.136, and the drop is concentrated at the strong-a1 end (deciles 8-9: -0.13, -0.24). Calling it 'goes up when the policy leans toward a2' simplifies this. Dropping the term costs about 0.03 (0.572 vs 0.602).

Leftover misses by previous trial are moderate, not large: GO after a1 S2 r +0.11 and after a1 S1 u +0.10 are under-predicted; GO after a2 S2 r is rewarded... corrected: GO after a2 S1 r -0.11 and D1 after a2 S1 r -0.10 are over-predicted. Mean error is about 0.01 in every phase.

The late-episode D1 dips during unrewarded runs (worst windows: actual around -0.5, predicted around +0.35) are real and acknowledged in the label. Simple fixes barely help: (prev_reward==0)*ep_dec, its cubic version, and a 2-unrewarded-run term at D1 each add at most about 0.02, and no variant within 8 terms beat 0.6016 on test.

Checks that held up: GO S2 +0.35, rare +0.19, rewarded -0.33 / -0.26, D1 S1-unrewarded -0.22, D2 a2 +0.11 all match the fitted weights and the residual tables. GO terms alone give test 0.46. Adding trial-before terms does not help (0.58 or lower). No future variables are used.
